card.summary: The Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize and update the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program. It directs the Secretary to provide technical assistance and funding to eligible electric utilities to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies and share threat information, authorizing appropriations of $250,000,000 for fiscal years 2027 through 2031.

summary: The Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act reauthorizes a Department of Energy program through fiscal year 2031 that provides cybersecurity grants, technical assistance, and funding to certain rural and municipal electric utilities. It allows funding to be awarded on a competitive or noncompetitive basis, adds entities that operate defense critical electric infrastructure to the priority list, and protects all information shared under the program from disclosure under federal, state, tribal, or local freedom of information laws.

affected_groups.effect: May receive technical assistance, grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes on a competitive or noncompetitive basis to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies.
affected_groups.group: Rural electric cooperatives and municipal or small investor-owned electric utilities

affected_groups.effect: Must maintain the cybersecurity assistance program, establish award criteria, inform eligible entities of opportunities, and prioritize specific categories of utilities.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program through the period of fiscal years 2027 through 2031 with an authorization of appropriations of $250,000,000.
Permits the Department of Energy to provide technical assistance and award funding on either a competitive or noncompetitive basis.

Requires priority for funding and technical assistance to be given to eligible entities with limited cybersecurity resources, those owning assets critical to bulk-power system reliability, and those that own or operate defense critical electric infrastructure.

Exempts all information shared by or with the federal government or state, tribal, or local governments under the program from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act and similar state, tribal, or local open records laws.
missing_information: Specific funding allocations per fiscal year beyond the overall total authorized amount.
Detailed criteria the Secretary will use to determine which entities have limited cybersecurity resources.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act reauthorizes a Department of Energy program through fiscal year 2031 that provides cybersecurity grants, technical assistance, and funding to certain rural and municipal electric utilities. It allows funding to be awarded on a competitive or noncompetitive basis, adds entities that operate defense critical electric infrastructure to the priority list, and protects all information shared under the program from disclosure under federal, state, tribal, or local freedom of information laws.
summary_detail.significance: The bill continues and updates federal support for cybersecurity in smaller and rural electric utility networks, adjusting how funds are distributed and broadening the legal protections for shared cybersecurity data.
